summary: Implementation cleanly adds NETLOC_TO_SOURCE, _resolve_source_name, _fetch_rss_entries, _fetch_mattel_entries, and SOURCES per Decision 4. Named functions (not lambdas), per-feed error isolation, explicit field selection for FeedParserDict normalisation, and case-insensitive netloc lookup are all correct. One minor dead-code finding.

findings.description: Module-level constant _RSS_ENTRY_FIELDS = ('link', 'title', 'published', 'summary') is defined but never referenced. The field list is already explicit in the dict literal inside _fetch_rss_entries, so the tuple is dead code — it documents intent redundantly with the surrounding comment and the dict itself.
findings.recommendation: Remove the _RSS_ENTRY_FIELDS tuple; the preceding comment + the explicit dict literal already document the field set. Alternatively, drive the dict construction from the tuple (item = {k: entry.get(k, '') for k in _RSS_ENTRY_FIELDS}), but that obscures the per-field default ('' vs None for link) and hurts readability. Prefer removal.

good_practices_noted: Named fetcher functions (not lambdas) keep stack traces readable — matches patterns.md guidance.
Per-feed try/except with continue prevents one bad feed from aborting the whole registry — matches existing job() error isolation at L431-438.
Explicit field selection avoids leaking feedparser internals (summary_detail, title_detail, links) into pending_articles JSON — matches task-file edge-case #5.
Defensive urlparse try/except in _resolve_source_name — never raises even for weird input.
WARNING log on unknown netloc includes both link and feed URL for operator triage.
NETLOC_TO_SOURCE docstring block explains Decision 4 rationale (why explicit map vs bare-netloc inference).
